::: {.spotlight}

### Carceral Ecologies
[Partner: UCLA Institute for Society and Genetics (Nicholas Shapiro)]{.partners}

DSC staff and DataSquad students cleaned and integrated the lab's helicopter
flight data, provided GIS support, refactored the R code, and moved the analysis
onto DSC computing as the lab acquired larger datasets. A student researcher on
the project first learned R and GIS from DSC staff in a 2019 African American
Studies course taught with DSC, then worked with DSC and DataSquad more than 30
times in 2022.

> *"This work wouldn't have happened without your team!"*
> — Nicholas Shapiro, director of Carceral Ecologies, November 2024 (quoted with permission)

[**Outcome:** one measured piece of the work cut the time to load the data from about 318 minutes to about 2, about 159 times as fast. The research and its findings belong to the lab; Shapiro received a 2024 UCLA Public Impact Research Award for it.]{.impact}

:::

::: {.spotlight}

### BioCritical Studies Lab
[Partner: UCLA Institute for Society and Genetics (Terence Keel; Grace Sosa)]{.partners}

DataSquad students have worked on the lab's national deaths-in-custody dataset
since 2021: merging and reconciling sources, identifying missed deaths,
statistical comparisons, dashboards and maps, and integration code and a codebook
the lab uses to update the dataset itself.

> *"The work the DataSquad has done has helped us address this need and has allowed us to maintain this dataset over time and through revisions."*
> — Grace Sosa, assistant director, BioCritical Studies Lab, August 2024 (quoted with permission)

[**Outcome:** DSC contributed data integration, analysis, and visualization support to research later recognized through UCLA's 2024 Public Impact Research Awards.]{.impact}

:::

::: {.spotlight}

### Refugee Material Culture Initiative
[Partner: Professor Kelly Nguyen (Classics) and the Vietnamese Heritage Museum]{.partners}

Doug Daniels, DSC's emerging technologies librarian, 3D scanned the "Boat of
Hope," a river sampan that carried nine refugees out of Vietnam in 1984, and
prepared the models for the museum's digital exhibit. Student employee Bianca
Badajos helped set up the Potree viewer on pointcloud.ucla.edu, where the model
is hosted.

[**Outcome:** a public 3D model anyone can explore in a web browser ([Boat of Hope](https://www.pointcloud.ucla.edu/VHM/narrative_all.html)), which depends on DSC's continued hosting.]{.impact}

:::

Full accounts and sources: [Research Enabled by DSC](https://ucla-data-science-center.github.io/dsc-stats-reports/research.html#three-collaborations).
